confirmed_p0p1.title: Username/account enumeration oracle on admin forgot-password (distinct 400 vs 200 message) — kiosk login was hardened but this path was not
confirmed_p0p1.reproduction: Live :8780 with valid x-api-key (config/app.php:63 MIX_API_KEY). POST /api/auth/forgot-password {"email":"nope-xyz-99999@nowhere.test"} -> HTTP 400 {"errors":{"email":["Cet email n'existe pas."]}}. POST same with {"email":"admin@lecayenne.fr"} (real seeded user) -> HTTP 200 {"message":"Veuillez vérifier votre email pour le code."}. The 400-vs-200 + distinct body is a definitive existence oracle. Secondary corroboration: login endpoint POST /api/auth/login non-existent email ~0.225s vs existing-email+wrong-pw ~0.260s (Auth::attempt skips bcrypt when user absent) = ~35ms timing oracle on LoginController.php:68.
confirmed_p0p1.recommendation: Return an identical neutral 200 response ('Si cet email existe, un code a été envoyé') for BOTH existing and non-existing emails; perform the DB lookup + insert + dispatch only when the user exists but never branch the HTTP status/body on existence. Mirror the kiosk-login enumeration hardening. Add an enumeration sentinel test asserting status+body parity. For the login timing oracle, run a dummy Hash::check against a fixed bcrypt hash when the user is absent (constant-work) — but this is in LoginController, not frozen, safe to edit. Tighten forgot-password throttle to also key by lowercased email (like login-lockout RouteServiceProvider.php:247-266) so per-target attempts are bounded regardless of IP.

result.completeness_critic:
Default connection points to `foodking` (empty/wrong). The isolated DB is `foodking_2dot0`. The structural confirmation (grep: 0 vs 3 writes) is sufficient evidence — the DB probe is just for sizing. The finding stands on code analysis. Let me compile the final report.

## ULTRA-AUDIT — Hidden/Indirect/Reactive surface (completeness critic + new findings)

Spine `release/v1-integration @ 1dc5785a5`. Read-only, grep/Read-confirmed. The forgot-password enumeration oracle (already in your confirmed set) is independently re-verified real: `ForgotPasswordController.php:33` returns `400 'email_does_not_exist'` for unknown email vs `200 'check_your_email_for_code'` for known — distinct status AND message, throttle `3,60` IP-keyed only (route `routes/api.php:172-173`).

### NEW finding I can grep-confirm right now

**P2 — Asymmetric stock-release ledger: `stock_levels.on_hand` can be double-credited on cancel-then-refund (or refund-then-cancel) of the same order.**
- `app/Listeners/ReleaseStockOnOrderCanceled.php:15` and `ReleaseStockOnRefundCreated.php:15` both call `StockService::releaseForOrder($order, <reason>, ...)` with different `$reason` (`order_canceled` vs `refund`).
- `app/Services/Stock/StockService.php:349-440` (`releaseForOrderInTransaction`) is the dedup authority for the `on_hand` ledger. Its idempotency key embeds `$reason` AND `'released:'.$orderItem->released_qty.':delta:'.$deltaLineQty` (line 408-411). It **reads** `released_qty` (line 381) but **NEVER writes it** — confirmed: `grep -c "released_qty' =>|update.*released_qty|increment.*released_qty"` on StockService = **0**, on `AvailabilityService.php` = **3** (`:772` is the only writer).
- The EventServiceProvider comment (`EventServiceProvider.php:199`) explicitly claims OrderCanceled is "Idempotent via order_items.released_qty ledger inside AvailabilityService" — but that ledger only guards the **availability** path (`daily_consumed_qty`). The **StockService `on_hand`** path's only cross-event guard is the per-reason movement key. Because `order_canceled` and `refund` hash to different keys (`movementKey` line 327 includes `$reason`) and `released_qty` stays 0 from StockService's view, both events release the FULL line quantity → `on_hand` inflated by the order's stock requirements.
- Repro path exists: `OrderCanceled::dispatch` (PaymentService.php:825, OrderService.php:2226/2448, FrontendOrderService.php:816) and `RefundCreated::dispatch` (PaymentService.php:213, RefundWithCounterEntryService.php:436) can both fire for one order across its lifecycle. V1-LOCAL: not money/NF525 (stock count drift, self-corrects at next inventory) → **P2**, not blocking. Frozen-zone-free fix surface (StockService is not frozen).

### Surfaces the 8 lanes likely MISSED — concrete next-audit targets

1. **`app/Listeners/AwardLoyaltyPointsOnDelivery.php:103` vs `ClawbackLoyaltyPointsOnRefund` proportionality.** Award = `round($orderTotal * $rate)` on FULL total; clawback (`ClawbackLoyaltyPointsOnRefund.php:51`, `LoyaltyService::clawbackEarnedPoints:150`) claws back the **FULL** `loyalty_points_awarded` on ANY `RefundCreated`, including a **partial** refund. Clawback is per-order idempotent (`type='manual_deduct'` dedup) so it won't double-fire — but a partial refund (e.g. one item of a 5-item order) zeroes the WHOLE earned balance. Verify whether partial-refund flows pass `refundedItems` and whether clawback should be proportional. Not yet opened by the loyalty lane.

2. **`app/Console/Commands/Stripe/DrainStrandedCpnCommand.php` (scheduled `stripe:drain-stranded-cpn`, Kernel:238) — coverage gap, not correctness.** It flips only `Order` (CARD) to PAID via `PaymentService::payment()` (correct, fiscal-allocating). But kiosk Stripe orders are `FrontendOrder` — if a kiosk card payment strands, this command (Order-only `where`) never drains it. Trace whether any kiosk/FrontendOrder card path can strand. SYNC-CRON lane appears to have traced outbox crons but not this money cron's model coverage.

3. **Z auto-close/open cron timing drift (`Kernel.php:401` close `dailyAt('23:59')`, `:446` open `dailyAt('00:01')`).** Code = ~2-min orphan window; surrounding comments variously claim "23:55+00:05" (10-min) and "23:59:55+00:00:05" (10-sec). The window is bridged by `fiscal_alloc_error_at` + `foodking:fiscal:retry-alloc` (scheduled :266), so it's the accepted degraded path — but the **stale/contradictory comments** mean no one has re-verified the actual residual orphan window. Worth a fiscal-lane re-trace.

4. **`app/Observers/UserObserver.php:17` `updating()` → `setBranch()` on every User save** (`DefaultAccessModelTrait::setBranch:32`). Re-derives `branch_id` from `Auth::user()` on any update. Loyalty increments use query-builder (`User::where()->increment()`) which bypasses observers — safe. But verify no admin/staff User-edit flow silently rewrites `branch_id` (P3 single-box; would matter at V2 multi-tenant). SEC-AUTHZ lane likely audited controllers, not this model observer.

5. **Unverified reactive listeners no lane named:** `EscalateOutboxBroadcastSwallowed`, `RevokeTokensOnBranchDeactivated` (branch-deactivation → token revocation: confirm it can't revoke the single-box branch_id=1's own kiosk tokens), `NotifyStockLowOnStockLevelChanged` (threshold spam under the cancel/refund double-release above), and the FCM trio `SendFcmOnOrderCreated`/`SendFcmOnOrderStatusChange` (verify payload carries no customer PII to a misconfigured topic). None appear in the 8-lane confirmed set.

6. **`app/Jobs/CleanupStalePendingKioskOrders.php:143` dispatches `OrderCanceled` from a queued job** → triggers the full stock/availability release cascade asynchronously. Combined with finding #P2 above: a stale-kiosk auto-cancel that later gets manually refunded is a concrete realization of the double-release. Trace the SLA window (`CleanupStalePendingKioskOrders`) against refund eligibility.

Highest-value next step: open the **partial-refund loyalty proportionality** (#1) and the **StockService released_qty asymmetry** (P2) together — both live in non-frozen service code and share the refund cascade.
